name: Short Story
early_stage_explanation: The evidence supports early stage. The press release dated September 2026 and the company's own site say Short Story (drinkshortstory.com), an electrolyte drink mix, launched in 2026. It is sold direct-to-consumer and at local markets such as Denver's South Pearl Street Farmers Market, with retail only planned. It is family-founded by Danielle Nuss, her husband Oliver and her sister-in-law Suzanne, and nothing suggests a parent company. The independent search results (PitchBook, Tracxn, Fortune, CB Insights) describe a different company, Short Story / Short Story Box, a San Francisco clothing subscription startup founded in 2019 with Y Combinator and Tribe Capital backing. Those funding rounds don't apply to the electrolyte brand, so they don't contradict the agent's claim. No funding for the drink brand appears anywhere in the evidence, and its size, launch date and channels all fit an early-stage startup.
founders_supported_explanation: Danielle Nuss and Oliver Nuss are supported. LinkedIn lists both as Co-Founders, and the press release and about page back Danielle's role and origin story. Oliver is also named on the about page as Danielle's husband who is building the company with her. Suzanne's claim fails. The claim says the Instagram account names her as 'co-founder Suzanne', but the Instagram page never mentions Suzanne. The about page only says Danielle is building Short Story 'alongside her husband Oliver and her sister-in-law Suzanne'. It does not call Suzanne a co-founder. The photo caption 'The founders of Short Story together' does not say who is pictured. So no source shows Suzanne as a founder.

name: todo
early_stage_explanation: The evidence supports early stage. A PR Newswire release dated Sept 30, 2025 announces the launch of todo's RTD protein and fiber shakes, so the product launched recently. Distribution is DTC only via drink-todo.com, shipping to the US and Canada, with no retail partners mentioned. The company is led by a founder (Niket Soni) and is not described as part of a larger company. The independent search found no funding for this todo; the CB Insights (Todo Verde) and Tracxn (Todo Works) hits are different companies, and the retail funding pages are generic. The press logos are mostly paid press-release pickups. The '25,000+ customers' claim is unverified and a bit high for a launch about 6-9 months ago, and the 50% clearance sale suggests some inventory pressure, but neither indicates a priced round, national retail, or ownership by a larger company. Overall it fits the early-stage criteria.
founders_supported_explanation: Niket Soni's claim is supported. The about-us page names 'Niket, Founder & CEO' with the Biomedical Science and Nutrition background, and the low energy and digestive issues story. The PR Newswire and Yahoo Finance releases give the full name 'Niket Soni' as founder of todo / Drink Todo, so the cross-result link is reasonable. Christine's claim failed on the role. The claim says 'Co-founder', but the about-us page calls her 'Creative Director' and 'the creative mastermind'. It does list her under 'Meet the founders' on the collection page, but that text is cut off, so her title there is not visible. The description of her focus on storytelling, branding and creative strategy and her passion for health, wellness and travel matches the about-us page. However, the cited pages (the collection page and the Boxing Day sale page) do not contain that description, and the Boxing Day page does not mention Christine at all. Since the 'Co-founder' title is not confirmed in the cited sources and the supporting text sits on an uncited page, the Christine claim is only partially supported. She is shown as part of the founding team, not clearly as a co-founder, so the label is partially_supported rather than unsupported.

name: LĪNA (Lina Universal Balm)
early_stage_explanation: The evidence supports the agent's claim. LĪNA launched in May/June 2025 (press release May 3, 2025; Formes de Luxe says June 2025), so it is well within the last 2 years. It has a single product, the Universal Balm at $135, sold online DTC. A rollout into spas and private clubs is only planned. Press is limited to local outlets (VoyageLA, Shoutout LA, Fox Magazine) plus a PR Newswire release, and the awards are indie-level (Beauty Tank finalist, CertClean nomination). The founder, Lina Leikam, is a solo makeup artist, and the company is The LINA Group LLC, with no sign of a parent company. No funding appears for this brand; the Tracxn hits are for unrelated companies (Lina Stores, LiNa Energy). Because the Formes de Luxe article groups it with newly launched indie brands, this is a very early-stage, bootstrapped startup.
founders_supported_explanation: Both founders are shown in the sources. Lina Leikam is called Founder of LĪNA in the press release and the Fox Magazine piece. Thomas Leikam is listed as Co-Founder in the LinkedIn leadership section. One background detail for Lina Leikam fails: the sources never say she is an Esthetician. They support the Los Angeles base, German origin, barber school, work as a hairdresser in Berlin, the Beni Durrer Hair & Makeup Artistry diploma, and 13+ years in film, TV, editorial and commercial work. Thomas Leikam's claim has no background to check.

name: Sainte Labs
early_stage_explanation: The evidence supports the early-stage claim. Sainte Labs soft-launched on Oct 12, 2025, and the trade-press piece independently confirms an October 2025 launch, so it is well within the last 2 years. It is a small LLC founded by two makeup artists. It sells primarily DTC, with select best-selling SKUs on Amazon, so it has no national retail footprint. Both the press release and the Formes de Luxe article place it among newly launched indie brands, and it is described as small-batch, with about eight SKUs still in development. No evidence shows a priced VC round or parent-company ownership. The independent search returned only unrelated companies (Isigny Sainte, Sente, Sainte Anne, Sentient Labs), so it surfaced no funding for Sainte Labs. Beth Bender Beauty is a separate brand run by one founder, not a larger parent that owns Sainte Labs.
founders_supported_explanation: Both founders are shown as founders of Sainte Labs, but some background details are not in the sources provided. Beth Bender: the Digital Heroes page calls her "Co-Founder" who "runs Sainte Labs in Los Angeles". PRLog says the brand was created by "beauty industry veterans Beth Bender and Lia Robin". Two details failed: nothing provided calls her a make-up artist (PRLog mentions only "professional artistry" and "pro artist authority"), and the October 2025 launch date appears nowhere. Lia Robins: PRLog names "Lia Robin" (spelled without the s) as a creator alongside Beth Bender, which supports co-founding and the shared frustration with existing products. The make-up artist description is not stated, and the "Co-Founder" title is inferred from "created by". The Formes de Luxe article, cited for both founders, was not among the source pages, so the make-up artist and October 2025 details could not be checked against it.

name: Ayn Skin House
early_stage_explanation: The evidence supports early-stage. Formes de Luxe says Ayn Skin House, founded by Inam Fraihat, launched in July 2025 and has five products with two more in development. That puts the launch well within the last 2 years. The brand sells through its own Shopify-style site (aynskinhouse.com) with no retail distribution mentioned. Its Instagram has about 1,477 followers, which is a small footprint. No funding round, investor, or parent company appears in the evidence. The funding items from the independent search (OneSkin, EDJY, Slate and others) concern different companies. The UK Companies House record (incorporated 2022, retail not in stores) is not tied to Ayn by name and is most likely an unrelated entity, so it does not undermine the July 2025 launch. Being a Beauty Tank finalist shows some recognition but not outside funding or scale.
founders_supported_explanation: The cited Formes de Luxe article says "Ayn Skin House founded by Inam Fraihat", which backs both the name and the Founder role. The claim gives no background details, so there is nothing else to check. No claims failed.
